We observed an outage impacting our production integration with Redwood between 09:14 PDT and 09:36 PDT today (approximately 22 minutes). During that window our nightly payout job failed with connection errors to /v1/chat and /v1/generate endpoints; retries succeeded after the window.

Can you confirm Redwood's observed downtime for that interval, and whether this meets the SLA credit criteria? Our contract references a 99.95% uptime target with credit for sustained downtime beyond the threshold.

We also need a postmortem for this event and an ETA for when we can expect the formal report and credit calculation — this incident caused a delay to our settlement batch and we may need documentation for our internal auditors.

Attaching a short extract from our logs showing the 503 errors (attached as acme_503_excerpt.txt).

Marissa — preliminary update and incident summary below. Incident ID: INC-98431 (internal). Attaching a short preliminary report.

Summary / timeline (UTC times converted to PDT in parentheses):
- 2026-05-16 16:13:10 UTC (09:13:10 PDT): First error spike detected on the inference gateway for a subset of customer routes backed by pool-4.
- 2026-05-16 16:13:45 UTC (09:13:45 PDT): Autoscaler failed to provision a replacement node after a GPU driver OOM caused one pod to crash; small pool capacity dipped below minimum for ~22 minutes.
- 2026-05-16 16:35:30 UTC (09:35:30 PDT): Autoscaler completed remediation and traffic shifted back to healthy nodes.
- Impacted endpoints observed: /v1/chat, /v1/generate for routes routed to pool-4.

Root cause (prelim): a GPU driver OOM triggered container restarts; our autoscaling path did not reclaim capacity fast enough due to a transient provisioning timeout in the cloud provider API. We're continuing a deeper analysis on why the provisioning timeout occurred.

SLA implications: based on the confirmed downtime window (09:13:10 – 09:35:30 PDT, ~22 minutes), this exceeds the SLA threshold for credit per section 3.2 of the contract (see attached SLA excerpt). We will prepare the credit calculation per the contract formula and provide the amount and how it will be applied to your account.

Attachments: prelim_incident_report_98431.pdf (PDF) — includes timeline, traces, and next-step action items.

Next steps:
1) Complete full postmortem (ETA 72 hours) with root cause analysis, long-term mitigation plan, and action owners.
2) Compute SLA credit and share the calculation within 48 hours.
3) Provide a remediation timeline for autoscaler/provisioning hardening and an update on testing schedule.

If Acme needs the credit quicker for reconciliation, we can issue a provisional credit and reconcile after the detailed calculation.

— Rishi
